hook: Why does a hot drink cool down but never heat up by itself? ☕
body: Ray explains heat and temperature, and why heat always flows from hot to cold. Save this for your next coffee break.
first_comment: What's the longest your coffee has ever stayed hot? ☕👇

hook: How does electricity actually get to your lamp? 💡
body: Ray follows the current through a simple electric circuit and shows what is really flowing in the wire. Send this to your favorite electrician.
first_comment: Guess first: what is actually moving inside the wire? Then check the video 👇

hook: How does the sound of a guitar reach your ear with only air in between? 🎸
body: Ray explains how waves work: they carry energy, not matter. Sound is a pressure wave, and speed = frequency × wavelength. Save this for later.
first_comment: If you could see sound waves, what sound would you look at first? 👇

hook: Why does an ambulance siren sound high coming toward you and low going away? 🚑
body: Ray explains the Doppler effect: motion squeezes and stretches waves, so the pitch changes. It works for light too. Send this to a friend who loves cars.
first_comment: Where have you noticed this? Sirens, race cars, trains? 👇

hook: Why do you see lightning first and only hear thunder seconds later? ⚡
body: Ray compares the speed of light and the speed of sound, and shows how to count the distance to a storm. Send this to someone who hates thunderstorms.
first_comment: Next storm: count the seconds between flash and thunder, then tell us your number 👇

hook: Why can you see yourself in a mirror but not in a sheet of paper? 🪞
body: Ray explains the law of reflection: the angle in equals the angle out. Smooth surfaces make images, rough ones scatter light.
first_comment: Which surface at home is the best mirror that isn't a mirror? 👇

hook: Why does a straw look broken in a glass of water? 🥤
body: Ray explains refraction: light changes speed between materials, so it bends. Try this at home with a glass of water and tell us what you see.
first_comment: Try it right now with a glass and a pencil. Does yours look broken too? 👇

hook: How can plain white sunlight turn into a rainbow? 🌈
body: Ray shows dispersion: white light is a mix of colors, and each color bends by a different amount. Send this to someone who chases rainbows.
first_comment: Which color of the rainbow bends the most? Answer before you scroll up 👇

hook: Why does a balloon stick to the wall after you rub it on your hair? 🎈
body: Ray explains static electricity and electric charge: rubbing moves electrons, opposite charges attract. Save this and try it with a balloon.
first_comment: Have you ever shocked yourself on a doorknob? Tell us your best story ⚡👇

hook: Why do two magnets snap together without even touching? 🧲
body: Ray explains magnetism, poles and magnetic fields, and how a current in a coil makes an electromagnet. Send this to a friend with fridge magnets.
first_comment: What happens if you cut a magnet in half? Guess first 👇

hook: If gravity pulls everything down, why doesn't the Moon crash into Earth? 🌙
body: Ray explains gravity and orbits: an orbit is falling while moving sideways fast enough to miss the ground. Send this to a space fan.
first_comment: Are astronauts really weightless? Give us your answer, then watch the end 👇

hook: Why do you feel pushed against the door when a car takes a sharp turn? 🚗
body: Ray explains circular motion, centripetal force and inertia. The outward push you feel isn't a force. Send this to a friend who drives fast.
first_comment: Double the speed in a turn: how much more force do you need? 👇

hook: How can a giant steel ship float when a tiny steel nail sinks? 🚢
body: Ray explains pressure, buoyant force and Archimedes' principle: floating depends on average density. Save this for later.
first_comment: Would a steel ship float if it were a solid block? Tell us why 👇

hook: Why is ice so slippery and sandpaper so grippy? 🧊
body: Ray explains friction: rough surfaces, the friction coefficient and why static friction beats sliding friction. Send this to someone who just fell on ice.
first_comment: Where is friction your best friend, and where is it your enemy? 👇

hook: Why is a slow truck harder to stop than a fast bicycle? 🚚
body: Ray explains momentum and impulse: p = m·v, and why airbags work by making a stop last longer. Save this for your next physics exam.
first_comment: Would you rather be hit by a bowling ball at 1 m/s or a baseball at 40 m/s? Explain with momentum 👇

hook: How can a small push lift a heavy rock? 🪨
body: Ray explains levers, the fulcrum and torque: a longer arm means less force, but you push farther. Send this to someone who loves tools.
first_comment: Which lever do you use every day without noticing? 👇

hook: Does time really slow down when you move fast? ⏱️
body: Ray explains Einstein's relativity and time dilation with a light clock, and why GPS needs relativity to work. Send this to the friend who loves space.
first_comment: Does it blow your mind that GPS needs relativity? Tell us what you think 👇
